suite.name: Unified AOT/C++: 8 maintained and 16 ported dasProfile workloads
notes: All 24 workloads use the existing benchmarks target, executable and --aot-compare report.
All 64 registry cases passed a separate one-iteration smoke run; all 48 AOT/C++ timing cases passed five repetitions.
Compilation, preparation, instantiation and warm-up are excluded; ordinary allocation, GC and checksum verification remain timed.
Both interop lanes call the same separately compiled non-inlined AddOne function. NativeFunction::Bind now accepts its context-free signature directly.
The host case retains its NativeContext parameter and uses a direct scalar entry. Error propagation, logical frames and GC roots remain enabled.
Ported floating workloads use double and deterministic inputs; sorting is stable. SHA and iterative Fibonacci explicitly wrap at 32 bits.
Process resident counters include other workloads in the process; they are not standalone footprint or peak RSS.

comparison_to_previous.reason: Same machine, toolchain, Release configuration, 24 workload inputs, C++ kernels, timing settings and correctness contracts. The change replaces scalar binding adapters with direct entries and binds the unchanged AddOne kernel without a context shim.

suite.name: H5 five-backend steady workloads and reload lifecycle
notes: 24 common workloads comprise 8 maintained and 16 ported workloads; all five backends use the same input sizes and validated checksums.
Steady wall time excludes compilation and warm-up; current dispatch, safepoints, roots, external fields and ordinary GC remain enabled.
C++ arithmetic and field loops may simplify as a whole; their ratios do not predict a general JIT benefit.
Fresh-session counters include source/code preparation and first execution but exclude process startup and OS-cache misses.
dasProfile input preparation runs after loading and before first_execution_ns; its cost is excluded from first-workload and steady timing.
Independent-process startup/peak samples cover both complete source suites and both JIT tiers; the OS file cache may be warm.
Lifecycle pause covers validation/GC, instantiation, migration, deoptimization and publication. Per-edit mean and maximum pauses are both retained.
Framework refresh is not installed, so its measured duration is zero; functional refresh behavior is covered by regression tests.
Logical constant/debug payloads overlap read-only image bytes. Block contents exclude allocator page padding and OS debugger overhead.
Shared-process resident counters include previously initialized backends and LLVM; use independent-process compilation peaks for attribution.
Only Windows x64 was executed for this acceptance run; macOS and Linux implementations were not tested on those hosts.

The measured JIT/AOT ratios do not establish near-AOT performance or an aggregate optimized-tier gain. Many wall-time CVs exceed 10%; small aggregate differences are not established stable regressions.

comparison_to_previous.reason: The suite adds VM, both reloadable JIT tiers, lifecycle and independent-process startup; machine/build/measurement metadata must match before direct comparisons.
